# Seniors of NJ

> The home for older adults in New Jersey. Independent, plain-English guides to New Jersey senior benefits (ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, Stay NJ, PAAD, LIHEAP), Medicare, caregiving, housing, things to do and ways to learn, work and meet people. Every guide cites official sources and shows the date it was last updated. Not a government agency.

## Benefits & Money

- [ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ: the complete 2026 guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/property-tax-relief-nj/): One form unlocks all three of New Jersey's property tax relief programs for seniors. Here is who qualifies, how much you could get, and how to file the PAS-1 by November 2.
- [PAAD, Senior Gold and Medicare help: how NJ seniors save](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/prescription-and-bill-help/): One New Jersey application can cut your prescription copays to $5, pay your Medicare premium and add $225 a year for utilities. Here is who qualifies in 2026.
- [Social Security's 3.6% raise for 2027: what it means in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/social-security-2027/): Checks grow in January, but Medicare, the earnings test and your claiming age all shape what you actually keep. Plus how New Jersey taxes retirement income.
- [Food and utility help for New Jersey seniors: where to start](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/food-and-utility-help/): SNAP, senior meals, farmers market benefits, heating aid and free weatherization can all ease a tight budget. Here is how each works and how to apply this season.
- [Benefits for older veterans in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/veterans-benefits-seniors-nj/): Tax breaks, VA pension with Aid and Attendance, veterans homes and burial benefits for older New Jersey veterans and surviving spouses.
- [Working after 60 in New Jersey: jobs, training and your rights](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/working-after-60-nj/): Part-time work, paid training through SCSEP or a second career can all make sense after 60. Here is where to find help in New Jersey and how a paycheck affects Social Security, Medicare and taxes.
- [ANCHOR in New Jersey: what seniors get and how to file](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/anchor-program-nj/): ANCHOR pays New Jersey homeowners up to $1,500 and senior renters $700. If you are 65 or older and own your home, you have to file the PAS-1 yourself by November 2, 2026.
- [Senior Freeze in NJ: how the property tax reimbursement works](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-freeze-nj/): Senior Freeze pays you back when your property taxes rise above your base year. Here are the 2025 rules, the income limits and how to keep your base year safe.
- [Stay NJ: how the senior property tax benefit works](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/stay-nj/): Stay NJ aims to cover half of a senior homeowner's property taxes, up to $6,500. Here is who qualifies for 2025, how the math works and when payments arrive.
- [PAAD in New Jersey: $5 and $7 prescriptions for seniors](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/paad-nj/): PAAD cuts prescription copays to $5 for generics and $7 for brand names. Here is who qualifies in 2026, how it works with Medicare Part D and how to apply.
- [Senior Gold in NJ: prescription help above the PAAD limit](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-gold-nj/): Earn a little too much for PAAD? Senior Gold cuts what you pay for each prescription and caps your yearly costs. Here are the 2026 income ranges and how it works.
- [LIHEAP in New Jersey: help with heating and cooling bills](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/liheap-nj/): One application covers heating aid, monthly bill credits and medically necessary cooling. Here are the 2026 to 2027 income limits and how older adults can apply by mail.
- [Meals on Wheels in NJ: home-delivered meals by county](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/meals-on-wheels-nj/): If getting groceries or cooking has become hard, your county can deliver meals to adults 60 and older. Here is who qualifies, what it costs and who to call in each of New Jersey's 21 counties.
- [Free tax help for seniors in NJ: AARP Tax-Aide and VITA](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/free-tax-help-seniors-nj/): Trained volunteers prepare federal and New Jersey returns for free every winter. Here is who qualifies, how to find a site when they open and what to bring.

## Health & Medicare

- [Medicare 101 for New Jerseyans turning 65](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-turning-65/): The parts, the deadlines, the 2026 costs and the penalties that last a lifetime. Here is how to get Medicare right the first time, with a month-by-month plan and free help from SHIP.
- [Medicare Advantage or Medigap? How to choose in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/advantage-vs-medigap/): Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7. Here is how the two paths really differ, the New Jersey Medigap rules most people never hear about, and the questions to ask before you sign.
- [NJ FamilyCare and MLTSS: how Medicaid pays for long-term care](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicaid-mltss-nj/): Medicare does not pay for long-term care. In New Jersey, Medicaid's MLTSS program can, at home, in assisted living or in a nursing home. Here are the 2026 limits, the five-year look-back and how to apply.
- [Staying well in New Jersey: falls, checkups, hearing and more](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/healthy-aging-nj/): Free balance classes, the Medicare checkups you are already paying for, cheaper hearing aids, and where to turn in a heat wave or a hard month. A practical wellness guide for New Jerseyans 60 and up.
- [Hearing aids for older adults in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/hearing-aids-seniors-nj/): Over the counter hearing aids, what Medicare covers, and New Jersey programs that help pay for hearing aids and phones.
- [Affordable dental care for older adults in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/dental-care-seniors-nj/): Medicare pays for very little dental work. Here is what it does cover, what NJ FamilyCare includes, and where New Jersey seniors can find low-cost or free dental care.
- [Medicare open enrollment for 2027: what NJ seniors should check](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-open-enrollment-2027-nj/): You have until December 7, 2026 to change Medicare plans for next year. Here is what to look for in your plan's notice, how 2027 drug costs work, how PAAD and Senior Gold fit in, and where New Jersey residents get free help.
- [Preventing falls at home for seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/fall-prevention-nj/): A home safety checklist, free balance classes through New Jersey's county offices on aging, what to ask your doctor, what to do after a fall and who can help pay for grab bars or a ramp.
- [Chair yoga for seniors in New Jersey: benefits, safety and classes](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/chair-yoga-seniors-nj/): What chair yoga is, what the research says, who should check with a doctor first, a gentle routine to try at home, and where to find classes across New Jersey.
- [Exercise at home for seniors in New Jersey: a safe weekly plan](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/exercise-at-home-seniors-nj/): How much activity older adults need, simple strength, balance and stretching moves for home, a sample week, when to stop, and what Medicare and New Jersey programs cover.
- [Staying active and engaged at home after surgery or rehab in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/active-after-surgery-nj/): How Medicare covers therapy at home and at the clinic, how to stick with the therapist's plan, prevent a fall and keep the mind busy during recovery, and who in New Jersey can help.
- [When a parent leaves the hospital: a New Jersey family guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/hospital-discharge-nj/): Observation versus inpatient, the 3-day rule for rehab coverage, how to appeal a discharge, and a checklist for the day your parent comes home.
- [NJ FamilyCare for seniors: the Aged, Blind, Disabled programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-familycare-seniors/): New Jersey's Medicaid program has its own path for people 65 and older. Here is how the Aged, Blind, Disabled programs work, the 2026 limits and how to apply.
- [Staying safe in a New Jersey heat wave: cooling centers and help](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/cooling-centers-nj/): Heat is hard on older bodies. Here is how to find a cooling center in your county, warning signs of heat stroke, and help with cooling costs.
- [Medicare Advantage or Medigap in NJ: how plans differ by county](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/medicare-advantage-vs-medigap-by-county-nj/): Medicare Advantage choices depend on the county you live in. Medigap mostly does not. Here is how to compare what is really available at your address, with free help from NJ SHIP.

## Caregiving

- [How to talk with a parent about getting help at home](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/first-conversation-about-care/): A practical guide for adult children in New Jersey: the signs it is time, how to open the conversation, what to avoid, and the first calls to make.
- [Help for family caregivers in NJ: respite, leave and support](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/caregiver-respite-nj/): New Jersey helps pay for breaks, adult day care and paid leave for people caring for an older relative. Here is who qualifies, what it covers and how to apply.
- [Things to do with a parent who has dementia](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/activities-for-dementia-nj/): Simple ways to spend good time together, adjusted for each stage of dementia, plus memory cafes and help for New Jersey families.
- [Can I get paid to care for my parent in New Jersey?](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/get-paid-caregiver-nj/): NJ FamilyCare's Personal Preference Program, VA programs, insurance and private agreements can pay a son or daughter for care. Here is who qualifies and where to start.
- [Thanksgiving and the holidays with a parent who has dementia](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/holidays-with-dementia-nj/): Smaller gatherings, earlier meals and a quiet room can make the season gentler for everyone. Practical, kind advice for families, plus New Jersey help for the caregiver.
- [Is your parent still safe living alone in New Jersey?](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/parent-living-alone-nj/): The warning signs to watch for, how to raise the subject, who can assess your parent, what help at home costs in New Jersey and a step-by-step plan for what comes next.
- [Caregiver burnout in NJ: signs, respite and where to get help](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/caregiver-burnout-nj/): Feeling worn down from caring for a parent or spouse? Here are the warning signs, quick ways to lighten the load, and the New Jersey programs that give family caregivers real time off.
- [Sundowning in dementia: evening routines and help for NJ families](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/sundowning-dementia-nj/): Late-day confusion and agitation are common in dementia. Here is what tends to set it off, routines that calm evenings, when to call the doctor and where New Jersey families can get support.
- [Music and dementia: a practical guide for New Jersey families](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/music-and-dementia-nj/): What the research really says about music and memory loss, how to build a playlist that works, when to bring in a board-certified music therapist, what it costs in North Jersey and how to make a home visit go well.
- [How to vet someone coming into your parent's home in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/vetting-in-home-help-nj/): Aides, handymen, instructors and tutors: how to check a New Jersey license or registration, what background checks really cover, what to ask about insurance and references, how to pay safely and what to do if something feels wrong.
- [Caregiver support groups in New Jersey: where to find your people](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/caregiver-support-groups-nj/): Free groups for families caring for someone with dementia, Parkinson's, stroke or a long illness, in person, online and by phone, plus county and faith-based programs and tips for choosing a group that fits.
- [When to call a geriatric care manager, and what they actually do](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/geriatric-care-manager-nj/): A care manager is a professional guide for families facing aging, illness or a sudden crisis. Here is what they do, what to ask, and how to find a good one in New Jersey.
- [How to choose a home care agency in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/home-care-agency-nj/): What New Jersey law requires of home care companies, how to check a license in minutes, what care costs and who pays, and the questions that separate a good agency from a risky one.
- [After a dementia diagnosis: where New Jersey families can turn](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/dementia-support-nj/): Helplines, memory cafes, adult day and respite programs, safety steps and the legal planning to do now, for New Jersey families facing Alzheimer's or another dementia.
- [JACC in New Jersey: home care help for seniors not on Medicaid](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/jacc-nj/): Jersey Assistance for Community Caregiving helps older adults who need a lot of care stay at home, even if they earn too much for Medicaid. Here are the 2026 rules.
- [How to report elder abuse or neglect in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/report-elder-abuse-nj/): Who to call depends on where the person lives. Here is a calm, step by step guide to reporting worries about an older adult at home, in a nursing home or in assisted living.
- [Nursing home vs. memory care in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nursing-home-vs-memory-care-nj/): When dementia makes home unsafe, families usually weigh a memory care unit against a nursing home. Here is how they differ, what each costs, who pays and how to check quality.

## Housing & Legal

- [Aging in place in NJ: making your home safe and comfortable](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/aging-in-place-nj/): Room by room changes, what they cost, who can help pay and how to hire a contractor safely in New Jersey, from split-levels to shore condos.
- [Estate planning basics for New Jersey seniors](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/estate-planning-nj/): Wills, powers of attorney, advance directives, POLST, inheritance tax and probate, explained in plain English for New Jersey families.
- [Where to live next: senior housing choices in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/housing-options-nj/): From staying put to a continuing care community, here is what each option offers, what care costs in New Jersey, and what to ask before you sign.
- [Selling the family home in New Jersey: a downsizing guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/downsizing-nj/): A realistic timeline, how to sort a lifetime of belongings, and the New Jersey tax rules every older seller should know before listing.
- [What to do when a parent dies in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/when-a-parent-dies-nj/): A gentle checklist for the first days, weeks and months, from death certificates and Social Security to probate and NJ inheritance tax.
- [How to get a disability parking placard or plates in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-handicapped-parking-placard/): Who qualifies, which form to use, what it costs and where to send it. Plus the rules for temporary placards after surgery or an injury.
- [Assisted living vs. home care in NJ: costs and how to choose](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/assisted-living-vs-home-care-nj/): Stay home with paid help, or move to assisted living? Here is what each costs in New Jersey, who pays, and the questions that usually decide it.
- [What senior care costs in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-care-costs-nj/): Home care, adult day, assisted living and nursing homes, with the latest CareScout figures for New Jersey, how they compare nationally and how families pay.

- [Free and discounted things to do in New Jersey after 60](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/free-and-discounted-nj/): Park passes, half-price train rides, tuition-free college classes and free museums. Here is what New Jersey residents 60 and older can get for little or nothing, and how to claim it.
- [20 easy day trips in New Jersey, region by region](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/day-trips-nj/): Lighthouses, gardens, museums and wildlife drives, with honest notes on stairs, walking distances and the best season to go.
- [15 New Jersey museums and historic sites worth the drive](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-museums-guide/): From Edison's lab in West Orange to a battleship on the Delaware, here is what to see at each stop, how easy it is to get around, and what seniors pay.
- [New Jersey gardens and easy walks, with the benches and restrooms noted](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/gardens-and-easy-walks-nj/): Arboretums, iris beds, cherry trees and flat paths along the canal and the bay. Here is what the ground is like at each one, where to sit, and when to go.
- [The Jersey Shore after Labor Day: a town-by-town guide](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/nj-shore-off-season/): Quiet beaches, easy parking and boardwalks you can actually stroll. Here is what stays open, where beach wheelchairs and mats are, and how to get there without driving.
- [Piano lessons for seniors in New Jersey: how to start at any age](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/piano-lessons-seniors-nj/): What the research really says about learning piano after 60, what happens at a first lesson, how to choose a teacher and a keyboard, and where to find low-cost music classes around New Jersey.
- [Art classes for seniors in New Jersey: painting, drawing and clay](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/art-classes-seniors-nj/): How to start making art after 60, which medium to try first, what to buy, how to work around arthritis or low vision, and where older adults can find free and low-cost art classes in New Jersey.
- [15 places in New Jersey to take the grandkids](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/grandkids-day-out-nj/): Zoos, aquariums, farms and a battleship, chosen for children and grandparents alike. Here is where the benches, elevators and wheelchair rentals are, and what seniors pay.
- [Mahjong, canasta and bridge for seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/mahjong-bridge-seniors-nj/): Why table games are good company for the mind, how long each one takes to learn, where to find lessons and games in New Jersey, and how to keep playing at home, including with someone who has memory loss.
- [Holiday lights and events for older adults in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/holiday-events-seniors-nj/): A handful of long-running New Jersey holiday traditions, from Cape May's candlelight tours to a free lights display in West Orange, with notes on walking, seating and tickets.

## Living Well

- [Learn something new after 60: classes and lessons across New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/learn-something-new/): From Osher courses at Rutgers to piano lessons in your own living room, here is where older New Jerseyans can keep learning, and why stretching your brain is worth it.
- [Staying connected: how to beat loneliness in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/staying-connected-nj/): Loneliness is a health risk, and the U.S. Surgeon General has said so plainly. Here are the senior centers, volunteer roles, phone and visitor programs, and tech help that can bring more people into your week.
- [Scams targeting New Jersey seniors now, and how to shut them down](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/scams-nj/): Fake grandkids, fake toll bills, fake PSE&G shutoffs. Learn the scripts scammers use, the red flags that give them away, and exactly who to call in New Jersey if money is already gone.
- [Cooking classes for seniors in New Jersey, and easier cooking at home](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/cooking-classes-seniors-nj/): Kitchen safety, food safety, cooking for one or two, tools that are easier on sore hands, and the free and low-cost cooking and nutrition classes open to older adults across New Jersey.
- [Tech help for seniors in New Jersey: free classes and support](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/tech-help-seniors-nj/): Smartphones, tablets, video calls and patient portals made simpler, plus how to avoid online scams, where to get free tech help across New Jersey and how to lower your internet bill.
- [Driving later in life in New Jersey: safety, rules and options](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/driving-later-nj/): New Jersey's license rules, refresher courses that can trim points, the warning signs to watch for, and how to get around when it is time to drive less.
- [Pickleball after 60 in New Jersey: how to get started](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/pickleball-nj/): The paddle sport filling New Jersey's park courts is easy to learn, cheap to try and very social. Here is how to find a game, what to buy and how to avoid the common injuries.
- [Golf for seniors in New Jersey: county courses and discounts](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/golf-seniors-nj/): County golf courses across New Jersey sell senior cards that cut the price of every round. Here is what they cost, where to play a shorter round and how to stay comfortable on the course.
- [Activities for homebound seniors in New Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/activities-for-homebound-seniors-nj/): Can't get out much? Books by mail, friendly callers, online classes, safe exercise and rides for the odd outing can keep life full. Here is what New Jersey offers.
- [Gift ideas for older parents and grandparents in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/gift-ideas-older-parents-nj/): Theater nights, museum memberships, park passes, lessons at home and gifts of time. Holiday ideas for 2026 that favor experiences over more things to store.
- [How to stay active and social through a New Jersey winter](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/winter-in-nj/): Indoor walking spots, the gym benefit hiding in your Medicare plan, warming centers and the real risks of shoveling. A practical plan for the cold months.
- [Home Happenings: lessons and activities that come to your living room](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/home-happenings/): A New Jersey company that sends checked local pros to older adults' homes to teach music, art, yoga, cooking, games, tech and more, starting in Essex and Passaic counties.
- [When a parent stops driving in NJ: rides, ID and staying connected](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/parent-stops-driving-nj/): Signs it may be time, how to start the talk, the non-driver ID, every county paratransit number, NJ Transit options and how to keep your mom or dad active and social without the car.
- [Writing a parent's life story: memoir and legacy projects in NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/life-story-memoir-nj/): How memoir interviews work and what they typically cost, how to record your mom or dad yourself, free tools like the StoryCorps App, New Jersey library memoir programs and tips for a parent with memory loss.
- [Senior centers in Bergen County, NJ: locations, hours and programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-centers-bergen-county-nj/): Bergen County runs ten free senior activity centers with a weekday lunch, and many towns run their own. Here is where they are, how lunch and rides work, and how to make the first visit easier.
- [Senior centers in Essex County, NJ: locations, hours and programs](https://seniorsofnj.com/article/senior-centers-essex-county-nj/): Essex County serves lunch at its Cafe in the Parks sites, and towns from Newark to Livingston run their own senior centers. ## En español

- [ANCHOR, Senior Freeze y Stay NJ: la guía completa de 2026](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/alivio-impuestos-propiedad-nj/): Un solo formulario abre los tres programas de alivio del impuesto a la propiedad. Quién califica, cuánto podría recibir y cómo presentar el PAS-1 a más tardar el 2 de noviembre.
- [PAAD, Senior Gold y Medicare: cómo ahorrar en NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/ayuda-recetas-y-facturas-nj/): Una sola solicitud de Nueva Jersey puede bajar sus copagos de recetas a $5, pagar su prima de Medicare y darle $225 al año para servicios públicos. Aquí le explicamos quién califica en 2026.
- [Ayuda con comida y servicios públicos para mayores en NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/ayuda-comida-y-servicios-nj/): SNAP, comidas para mayores, beneficios para mercados agrícolas, ayuda con la calefacción y climatización gratuita pueden aliviar un presupuesto apretado. Cómo funciona cada programa y cómo solicitarlo esta temporada.
- [Medicare básico para quienes cumplen 65 años en Nueva Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/medicare-al-cumplir-65-nj/): Las partes, las fechas límite, los costos de 2026 y las multas que duran toda la vida. Aquí le explicamos cómo hacer bien lo de Medicare desde la primera vez, con un plan mes a mes y ayuda gratuita de SHIP.
- [Estafas que hoy apuntan a los mayores de Nueva Jersey y cómo pararlas](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/estafas-nj/): Nietos falsos, cobros falsos de peaje, cortes falsos de PSE&G. Conozca lo que dicen los estafadores, las señales de alerta que los delatan y a quién llamar exactamente en Nueva Jersey si ya perdió dinero.
- [NJ FamilyCare (Medicaid) para mayores: los programas ABD](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/nj-familycare-medicaid-mayores-nj/): El programa de Medicaid de Nueva Jersey tiene su propio camino para las personas de 65 años o más. Aquí le explicamos cómo funcionan los programas Aged, Blind, Disabled, los límites de 2026 y cómo presentar la solicitud.
- [Seguro Social 2027: el aumento del 3.6% y lo que significa en NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/seguro-social-2027/): Los cheques suben en enero, pero Medicare, el límite de ganancias y la edad a la que usted reclama afectan lo que realmente le queda. Además, cómo Nueva Jersey cobra impuestos sobre los ingresos de jubilación.
- [Cómo elegir una agencia de cuidado en casa en Nueva Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/agencia-cuidado-en-casa-nj/): Qué exige la ley de Nueva Jersey a las agencias de cuidado en casa, cómo verificar una licencia, cuánto cuesta y qué preguntar antes de contratar.
- [PAAD y Senior Gold: ayuda con medicamentos recetados en NJ](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/paad-senior-gold-nj/): Dos programas de Nueva Jersey bajan sus recetas a $5 y $7, o le cobran $15 más la mitad del resto. Quién califica en 2026, cómo encajan con la Parte D y cómo presentar la solicitud.
- [Ayuda para pagar la calefacción y la luz en NJ: LIHEAP y USF](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/liheap-calefaccion-nj/): Una sola solicitud puede pagar parte de su calefacción y bajar sus facturas de luz y gas cada mes. Límites de ingresos para la temporada 2026 a 2027 y cómo pedir la ayuda, también en español.
- [Inscripción abierta de Medicare 2027 en NJ: qué revisar](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/inscripcion-abierta-medicare-2027-nj/): Del 15 de octubre al 7 de diciembre de 2026 puede cambiar su plan de Medicare para 2027. Lo que cambia, qué revisar y dónde conseguir ayuda gratis en español en Nueva Jersey.
- [Respiro y apoyo para cuidadores familiares en Nueva Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/respiro-cuidadores-nj/): Cuidar a un ser querido cansa. Nueva Jersey ofrece programas de respiro, centros de día, licencia familiar pagada y apoyo en español. Quién califica en 2026 y cómo pedir ayuda.
- [Cómo prevenir caídas en casa: guía para Nueva Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/prevenir-caidas-nj/): Una lista para revisar la casa, clases gratis de equilibrio por medio de las oficinas del condado, qué preguntarle al médico, qué hacer después de una caída y quién ayuda a pagar barras de apoyo o una rampa.
- [¿Cuánto cuesta el cuidado de personas mayores en Nueva Jersey?](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/costo-cuidado-mayores-nj/): Lo que cuestan el cuidado en casa, el centro de día, la residencia asistida y el hogar de ancianos en Nueva Jersey, según los datos más recientes, y cómo ayudan Medicaid MLTSS y JACC.
- [Demencia en la familia: ayuda y apoyo en Nueva Jersey](https://seniorsofnj.com/es/apoyo-demencia-nj/): Líneas de ayuda en español, grupos de apoyo, centros de día, respiro, seguridad y los papeles legales que conviene firmar pronto, para familias de Nueva Jersey que viven con Alzheimer u otra demencia.
